skill.name: binary-analysis
skill.description: Analyze suspicious binary files with Ghidra-based static analysis workflows. The skill guides users through strings, imports, decompilation, indicators of compromise, and threat reporting without executing the sample locally.
skill.summary: Analyze suspicious binaries with safe static reverse engineering workflows.
skill.author: DeepBitsTechnology

security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives caused by defensive malware-analysis terminology and markdown formatting. The skill is prompt-only guidance for static binary analysis and repeatedly tells users not to execute suspicious files locally. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or executable command behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Remote upload requirement for binary samples
remediation.suggestion: State that users should only upload binaries they are authorized to analyze and should follow their organization's evidence-handling policy.

remediation.issue: Malware classification wording triggers marketplace scanners
remediation.suggestion: Keep the defensive context explicit near malware category lists and prompt templates to reduce false-positive review friction.

content.value_statement: Unknown executables can hide malware behavior that standard scans miss. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through safe static binary analysis and clear threat reporting.
actual_capabilities: Guides static analysis of Windows executable formats such as EXE, DLL, SYS, and SCR files.
Structures Ghidra-based review of strings, imports, exports, functions, and PE metadata.
Helps identify suspicious APIs, persistence indicators, network artifacts, and anti-debugging patterns.
Produces threat assessment reports with severity, confidence, indicators, and recommended actions.
Supports defensive classification of suspicious binaries into malware categories when evidence supports it.
limitations: Requires access to suitable Ghidra or sandbox tools before deep analysis can run.
Does not safely execute suspicious binaries on the local system.
Packed, encrypted, or heavily obfuscated binaries may need separate unpacking work.
Findings depend on available artifacts and should be verified by trained security staff.

use_cases.title: Triage suspicious attachments
use_cases.description: Review an unknown executable from email or chat before deciding whether to quarantine, escalate, or dismiss it.

use_cases.title: Document incident artifacts
use_cases.description: Turn a recovered binary from a compromised host into a structured report with indicators and remediation guidance.

use_cases.title: Study malware behavior defensively
use_cases.description: Use decompilation, strings, imports, and suspicious API patterns to understand a sample without running it locally.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic binary review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage of one suspicious file
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the binary at [file_path] using safe static analysis. Summarize file metadata, strings, imports, exports, and any suspicious indicators.

prompt_templates.title: Review suspicious behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [binary] for suspicious behaviors such as registry changes, network communication, process injection, persistence, or anti-debugging. Explain the evidence for each behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Extract incident indicators
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [binary] and extract useful indicators of compromise, including hashes, domains, IP addresses, mutex names, registry paths, file paths, and notable strings.

prompt_templates.title: Create a full threat report
prompt_templates.prompt: Produce a complete threat assessment for [binary]. Include static analysis findings, decompiled behavior, suspected malware classification, confidence level, evidence, impact, and remediation recommendations.

output_examples.input: Analyze suspicious_setup.exe from a phishing email.
output: The report identifies file metadata, hashes, and suspicious imported APIs.
It highlights network indicators, registry persistence evidence, and risky process behavior.
It recommends isolation, endpoint scanning, indicator blocking, and escalation to incident response.

output_examples.input: Extract indicators from an unknown DLL found on a compromised server.
output: The analysis lists notable strings, exported functions, and embedded hostnames.
It explains which indicators are strong enough for detection rules.
It separates confirmed evidence from uncertain observations.

output_examples.input: Prepare an executive summary for a reverse engineering finding.
output: The summary states likely purpose, business impact, confidence, and recommended response.
Technical details are grouped separately for security teams.
The report avoids claiming malware classification without supporting evidence.

best_practices: Analyze suspicious files only in an isolated and authorized environment.
Record hashes, timestamps, strings, imports, and evidence for repeatable review.
Separate confirmed behavior from hypotheses and assign a clear confidence level.
anti_patterns: Do not execute an unknown binary on your workstation to see what happens.
Do not treat a malware family label as confirmed without specific evidence.
Do not upload sensitive or third-party binaries without authorization.

faq.question: What file types does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on binary formats such as EXE, DLL, SYS, BIN, OCX, SCR, CPL, and DRV files.

faq.question: Does this skill run malware samples?
faq.answer: No. It emphasizes static analysis and instructs users not to execute suspicious binaries locally.

faq.question: What tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects access to Ghidra-style analysis tools or a safe sandbox workflow for uploaded binaries.

faq.question: Can it prove a file is safe?
faq.answer: No. It can reduce uncertainty, but analysts should verify results with other tools and procedures.

faq.question: Can it extract indicators of compromise?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides extraction of hashes, strings, domains, IP addresses, registry paths, and related artifacts.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It is intended for authorized security analysts, incident responders, and researchers handling suspicious files.
